about: A sampled input whose source never names its shape.

files.model.yaml:
dsl: 1
model: tiny
title: Unnamed shape
currency: USD

nodes:

  request_rate:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: request/second
    distribution: {triangular: {minimum: 100.0, likely: 200.0, maximum: 600.0}}
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the busy hour, as the owners estimate it"}

  service_demand:
    kind: input
    decided: outside
    unit: core*second/request
    value: 0.02
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "processor time per request, as stated for this case"}

  cores:
    kind: input
    decided: you
    unit: core
    value: 16
    provenance: {kind: assumption, source: "the fleet chosen for this case"}

  busy_cores:
    kind: derived
    unit: core
    formula: request_rate * service_demand

  utilisation:
    kind: derived
    unit: dimensionless
    formula: busy_cores / cores

outputs:
  - utilisation
files.scenarios/reference.yaml:
scenario: reference
title: Reference
because: the model as declared
samples: 1000
seed: 20260916
overrides: {}

provenance.source: the fleet chosen for this case
the busy hour, as the owners estimate it
processor time per request, as stated for this case

problems.message: _builder_conformance/shape-not-named/model.yaml: input 'request_rate' is sampled as a triangular and its provenance never says so. The shape is a claim about what can happen — that a price cannot go negative, that a count has a hard maximum — and it is the claim a reviewer should argue with first. Name it in the source and say why (ch13, appendix C).
